name: manual_a60aaa
claim: Where pins live decides whether a generation pointer gives real rollback: when pins are in the package file, any pin change is a new consumer commit and takes the full ceremony because the harness drift guard forbids package-file changes between consumer and harness; a pointer that only validates repeated pins makes labels honest, while rollback without a consumer change needs the install to read a constraints file selected by the active generation, so inventory every file that repeats a pin and choose that option explicitly.

decisions.notes: Inventory on oramasys main after the M1 generation-2 merge: the promoted Core pin repeated in 13 files and the consumer commit and registry ref in 8 and 9; tests, not a generator, kept them equal. Design: .agent/references/virtual-versioning-generations-design.md.
